prize_parts.citation: For an uncompromising body of fiction that dissolves ordinary psychology, space and causality into dream logic and reinvents the perception of narrative in Chinese.

statement.case_for: My configuration does not change: Can Xue remains my final proposal, with Cărtărescu and Carson as alternatives. The round-1 exchange produced no new reading of her work that would move me, and I will not move merely to produce a four-vote majority. Under the common criteria the case is this. The voice is distinctive and hard to mistake for another writer's. The formal achievement is a dream logic that replaces realist psychology and causal plot and is kept as a working principle, not applied as decoration. The project has imaginative and intellectual depth, with her critical writing as supporting evidence only. The citation should rest on the fiction, and the single-writer scope is clean because the contribution is one personal narrative method. The chair asks what would answer the repetition-versus-variation doubt. I cannot supply a verified answer from a reading of the full corpus. What I can say is that the doubt has been put to Can Xue and Cărtărescu in nearly the same form, and no member has shown it to fall more heavily on one than on the other. Given that symmetry, I let the case for formal rigour and compression decide, and I hold that judgment provisionally. I do not treat the fact that all six members place her first or second as literary evidence. It only means the objections can be tested openly.
statement.case_against: The strongest reservation is unchanged and unresolved. A method held this constant may show sustained invention, or it may show a narrow and in places hermetic range, and from public knowledge and translated samples I cannot say which. Corpus coverage in translation is partial, and I cannot judge the Chinese prose directly. I also have no verified account of whether the longer novels carry the invention of the best short fiction as well. If the committee concludes that the later work only restates the earlier, or that opacity limits the significance of the whole oeuvre, my case weakens considerably and Cărtărescu becomes the better-grounded recommendation. Carson is a further alternative, but her hybrid and book-object work raises its own unresolved question about how much of it counts as literature within the framework of Nobel's will.

responses.point: Mattson keeps Cărtărescu first and says that if a reading across his later volumes showed his work thinning, she would reconsider and move Can Xue to first. She treats the repetition concern about him and the hermeticism concern about Can Xue as comparable.
responses.response: I accept her framing that the two risks are comparable, and that is the reason I hold Cărtărescu as my first alternative and not as a lesser one. I still read the costs differently. A repeated motif in a very long cycle costs more than a consistent method in a more compressed body of work, because length has to be earned. But that is my judgment from translations and public knowledge, and I do not claim to have settled it. I agree with her proposed test of reading the later volumes and not only the best-known novels, and I would apply it to Can Xue's longer fiction in the same way. If the committee cannot run that test on both writers, my reading rests on formal discipline over scale, and I say that openly.

responses.point: Sem-Sandberg separates recurrence of motif used as structure, as in a trilogy circling one body and one memory, from recurrence as thinning. He suggests a Cărtărescu citation that centres the novels, with the poetry as a foundation and not an equal pillar.
responses.response: The distinction between structural and exhausted recurrence is the useful one, and I wish to apply it to both writers. I cannot say in which category Cărtărescu's later volumes fall, and I would not claim to know it for Can Xue's longer works either. His proposal on citation scope is sound and brings the claim closer to what the committee has actually read. If the committee moved to Cărtărescu, I would prefer a citation centred on the novels, which is where our shared reading is thickest. This is the main reason he is my first alternative. I still stay with Can Xue, but I accept that this is a close judgment and that Sem-Sandberg's reading of his wider range is a legitimate one.

responses.point: Olsson, as chair, argues that Zurita's case can rest on the language and architecture of Purgatory and Anteparadise, with the sky-writing and desert works as context only. He asks for regional and Spanish-language expert input on whether the later volumes sustain the early intensity.
responses.response: My round-1 hesitation about Zurita was partly practical, and the chair's answer addresses part of it: a citation limited to the books would settle what the prize honours. It does not settle my other difficulty, which is that I cannot assess the sound and syntax of Spanish poetry from partial translated selections. I therefore do not move Zurita above my alternatives. I agree that expert input would be a better basis than my impressions. I also agree that difficulty of translation is not an argument against the poems. It only means my confidence in my own judgment is lower, and I have not ranked him above the others for that reason alone.

responses.point: Swärd keeps Can Xue first and sets herself a harder standard: if no one can point to real variation inside the method, or if opacity runs through the whole oeuvre, she would reconsider the order of Can Xue and Cărtărescu.
responses.response: I share that standard and accept it for myself. Her point that agreement among members who share the same description is not an independent check is correct, and I have tried not to treat it as one. On Robinson, whom she holds second, I continue to rank her below Can Xue for breadth and not for quality. The sentence-level control and the Gilead sequence are real. The question for a whole-oeuvre citation is whether the claim reaches beyond one deeply explored world, and for me it does so more clearly with a method that reinvents narrative perception. I am not certain of that comparison, and it is a difference of judgment.

uncertainties: I cannot assess Can Xue's Chinese prose directly, and how far the translated voice matches the original is unresolved.
Corpus coverage in translation is partial, so sustained quality across the whole output, including the longer novels, is not verified.

Whether a very consistent dream-logic method deepens over time or repeats cannot be settled from the supplied descriptions. The same test applies to Cărtărescu's later volumes, and I have no evidence-based answer to either.
My judgments of Cărtărescu, Carson and Zurita rest on translated selections and public knowledge. I have not independently verified any text.
How hybrid and book-object work (Carson) or landscape-scale interventions (Zurita) count under the framework of Nobel's will remains undecided.
The ordering of Can Xue and Cărtărescu is a close judgment that could reasonably go the other way.
statement.conflict_note: None apparent from the supplied profile. My biography of Selma Lagerlöf, my own fiction and my interest in parallel structures, ekphrasis and myth are context only. They are not evidence of preference for any shortlisted writer, and no documented professional tie to any of them is recorded. Conflicts are disclosed here and not adjudicated.
